source.title: Gain modulation in the central nervous system: where behavior, neurophysiology, and computation meet.

confidence_rationale: Gain modulation is widespread and, across a POPULATION of gain-modulated units read out downstream, supports a general class of computations (coordinate transforms, invariant responses). That is, population-level gain can change the input-output mapping, not only its magnitude. This undercuts ARC-111's discriminator premise that 'a gain model can rescale a fixed policy but cannot REORDER it', which holds only when gain is applied to a single output scalar. Supports the claim's view that context-dependence needs more than output gain, so mixed.
failure_signatures: Gain applied to many hidden units followed by a fixed readout can implement context-dependent mappings, including reorderings, so 'reordering' does not by itself discriminate weight-form from gain-form conditioning.
The review concerns fast, input-driven gain fields (e.g. eye position), not learned context-indexed weights, so it neither supports nor directly tests ARC-111's learned-weight mechanism.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Gain modulation, in which one input changes a neuron's sensitivity to another without changing its selectivity, is found in many cortical and subcortical areas; gain-modulated neurons can serve as a basis for a general class of computations, namely coordinate transformations and invariant responses.
mapping.ree_translation: Bears directly on ARC-111's falsifier. The claim's control arm assumes context-varying gain over a fixed weight set can only rescale, so any context-dependent REORDERING of committed channels must come from the weight form. Salinas & Sejnowski show that with gain on a population of basis units and a downstream readout, gain alone implements nonlinear, context-dependent mappings. Whether REE's gain form can reorder depends on where the gain sits: on a single per-channel output (cannot reorder) or on a hidden population (can).
mapping.mapping_caveat: REE's current gain forms (MECH-152 terrain_weight, ARC-016 precision, MECH-261 write gating) are mostly scalars on output or on a channel, not gain fields over a basis population, so for the shipped substrate the claim's discriminator may still hold. The caveat is about the discriminator's generality, not the current code.
mapping.source_context: Review linking parietal gain fields, attentional modulation and computational basis-function models.

confidence_components.notes: Classic review; key value is methodological -- it constrains how the ARC-111 falsifier must be built.
